entities.summary:
São Paulo is the capital city of the state of São Paulo and the most populous city in Brazil, South America, and the Southern Hemisphere, with 12.3 million in the city and 22 million in the metropolitan area. Founded by Jesuit missionaries in 1554, São Paulo transformed from a small colonial settlement into one of the world's great megacities through coffee wealth in the 19th century and industrial expansion in the 20th.

The Jesuits founded the Colégio de São Paulo de Piratininga on January 25, 1554 — an evangelical mission post in the Serra do Mar highlands. The town remained a modest backwater for three centuries. The coffee boom (1850s–1930s) brought a massive transformation: São Paulo became the hub of Brazil's coffee economy, attracting millions of European immigrants — particularly Italians (over 1 million), Spanish, Germans, and Japanese — who created the cosmopolitan industrial working class. By 1900, São Paulo was the fastest-growing city in Latin America.

Industrialization under Getúlio Vargas (1930s) and the subsequent economic miracle (1950s–1970s) made São Paulo the industrial heartland of South America — home to the auto industry, petrochemicals, and Brazil's financial sector. The ABC Paulista industrial suburbs were the birthplace of Brazil's independent labor movement under Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (elected president 2002 and 2022). São Paulo's cultural life — the São Paulo Biennial (founded 1951, the world's second-oldest art biennial), the carnival and music scene — gives it global cultural significance beyond its economic weight.
